title: Limits preserve compatible levelwise isomorphisms
statement:
If $u_n:M_n\to N_n$ is a compatible map of towers and every $u_n$ is an
isomorphism, then $R\varprojlim u_n$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: By the definition of the sequential derived inverse limit, a compatible map of towers acts componentwise on the two product terms and therefore induces a morphism between the corresponding Roos triangles. The component maps are all isomorphisms by hypothesis, so the product map is an isomorphism. Applying the existing levelwise-isomorphism lemma [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] to this morphism of Roos triangles yields that the induced map on derived inverse limits is an isomorphism.
